    Home / Docs / Credits and usage

    Credits and usage

    Read your balance, your spending limits and the usage behind a bill.

    Use this page to read your balance, your spending limits and the usage behind a bill. Money is held in wallets and counted in mu, the unit of account.

    Read your balance and spending

    Today the balance and the spending page are session endpoints of the console, not relay-key endpoints:

    GET /api/me/wallets

    Authentication signed-in session; roles: admin, cfo_viewer, fde, hr_ops, manager, member, operator

    A wallet has a balance and an amount held. A spending cap has a period, a limit, what is spent so far, and a forecast of the day it runs out. A person can pause spending, and the page lists the runs a pause skipped.

    What happens when a budget runs out

    Budgets degrade before they block. When a budget runs out the router first lowers autonomy or files a request for help; a hard stop comes after. When a request does stop for money it answers 402; see Errors.

    Read usage with your relay key

    Four read-only endpoints under /v1 take the relay key itself as the bearer, exactly as the completion endpoints do. A revoked, expired or unknown key is refused with the same 401 as everywhere else. They read the key's own ledgers: a decision of another key or another workspace is a 404, never a 403. Each costs one request against the key's rate limit.

    curl
    curl https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/key -H "Authorization: Bearer mrk_<prefix>_<secret>"

    Key

    GET /v1/key

    Authentication relay key (bearer)

    Example request

    curl
    curl https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/key \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_KEY"
    Python
    import os, requests

r = requests.get(
    "https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/key",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['RELAY_KEY']}"},
)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json())
    TypeScript
    const r = await fetch("https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/key", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RELAY_KEY}` },
});
if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status} ${await r.text()}`);
console.log(await r.json());

    Response

    FieldTypeDescription
    object requiredstringThe kind of object returned, for example chat.completion. Always "key".
    id requiredstringThe answer's id.
    prefix requiredstring
    scopes requiredarray of string
    budgetEnvelopeId requiredstring or null
    expiresAt requiredstring or null
    createdAt requiredstring
    lastUsedAt requiredstring or null
    unit requiredstring Always "mu".
    spendMu requiredintegermicro-dollars, the unit of account
    period requiredobject
    period.from requiredstring
    period.to requiredstring
    Example response (shape)
    {
  "object": "key",
  "id": "<id>",
  "prefix": "<prefix>",
  "scopes": [
    "<scopes>"
  ],
  "budgetEnvelopeId": "<budgetEnvelopeId>",
  "expiresAt": "<expiresAt>",
  "createdAt": "<createdAt>",
  "lastUsedAt": "<lastUsedAt>",
  "unit": "mu",
  "spendMu": 0,
  "period": {
    "from": "<from>",
    "to": "<to>"
  }
}

    Returns the key's id, prefix, scopes, budget envelope, expiry, and what it spent this calendar month in mu. Never the hash.

    Usage

    GET /v1/usage

    Authentication relay key (bearer)

    Example request

    curl
    curl https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_KEY"
    Python
    import os, requests

r = requests.get(
    "https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/usage",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['RELAY_KEY']}"},
)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json())
    TypeScript
    const r = await fetch("https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/usage", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RELAY_KEY}` },
});
if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status} ${await r.text()}`);
console.log(await r.json());

    Returns the rollup of the key's ledger rows for a period: requests, tokens and cost. from and to take an ISO date or datetime (default: this UTC calendar month). end_user narrows to one end-user tag, and group_by=end_user returns one row per tag.

    curl
    curl "https://api.massrelay.ai/v1/usage?group_by=end_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer mrk_<prefix>_<secret>"

    Read the rate-limit headers

    Every /v1 answer whose request reached the rate limiter carries the state of the limit that binds that key, read from the same evaluation that admitted the request, so a header never costs a second slot.

    • **X-RateLimit-Limit** — requests per minute of the binding limit (the key's, or its workspace's if that is tighter).
    • **X-RateLimit-Remaining** — whole requests still admitted right now without being queued.
    • **X-RateLimit-Reset** — seconds, rounded up, until one more request would be admitted without queueing (0 while some remain).
    • **Retry-After** — on a 429 only: seconds to wait, rounded up.

    When no limit is configured for the key or its workspace, the three X-RateLimit-* headers are not sent. The same headers ride on streamed answers and on the 429. See Limits for how limits are applied.
